92e81f6d573e7da6.title: Mechanical quote check accepts gap-heavy or very short segments, so a fabricated quote can still pass as OK

history.note: first observed
remediation recorded; pending verification by re-audit: Quotes that skip lines with '...' must contain at least 12 checkable characters, or they are UNCHECKABLE instead of OK.

re-audit verified the fix: quote_matches now returns None when the quote contains an elision ("..." or an ellipsis character) and its checkable segments total fewer than 12 characters. check_item turns None into UNCHECKABLE_QUOTE, which is in the UNCHECKED set, so these quotes no longer count as OK. Segments under 3 characters are dropped before the count. I could not run the code, so this rests on reading it. A gap-heavy quote with 12 or more checkable characters is still allowed, as the note describes. A quote whose only gaps are [REDACTED] markers is not covered by the 12-character floor, because only elisions trigger it. That is a narrower, separate case.

remediations.note: Quotes that skip lines with '...' must contain at least 12 checkable characters, or they are UNCHECKABLE instead of OK.

36a86acf42d3e01f.title: CI installs jsonschema without a lockfile, so transitive Python dependencies float; the npm install is pinned only at the top level

history.note: first observed
not observed in an assessed domain; confirm resolution
remediation recorded; pending verification by re-audit: CI installs test tools from tools/ci-requirements.txt with exact versions and sha256 hashes (--require-hashes).

verifier reports the fix is not effective: The Python half of the finding is fixed. ci.yml line 30 installs with `--require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -r tools/ci-requirements.txt`. The requirements file pins seven entries with sha256 hashes, including the transitive packages attrs, referencing, rpds-py, jsonschema-specifications and typing-extensions, with per-Python-version markers. The finding's title also says the npm install is pinned only at the top level. That is still true: ci.yml line 54 runs `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.289`, and I found no lockfile, `npm ci` or integrity pin. This is tracked as supply-chain.S1. Mark the finding fixed only if the owner accepts and documents the npm residual risk, or commits a lockfile for the CI tool.
remediation recorded; pending verification by re-audit: npm half fixed: CI installs Claude Code with npm ci from tools/ci-npm/package-lock.json (integrity-pinned); pip half was already hash-locked.

re-audit verified the fix: Both halves are locked. The pip install uses --require-hashes and --only-binary with tools/ci-requirements.txt. That file pins all 6 distinct packages, with environment markers for the Python-version-specific ones, and each carries a sha256 hash. The npm install uses npm ci against tools/ci-npm/package-lock.json, which has integrity entries. The package.json pins version 2.1.289.

remediations.note: CI installs test tools from tools/ci-requirements.txt with exact versions and sha256 hashes (--require-hashes).
npm half fixed: CI installs Claude Code with npm ci from tools/ci-npm/package-lock.json (integrity-pinned); pip half was already hash-locked.
